claim: Cassis was one of the first AOCs in France, established in 1936 when the AOC system was put in place, with each vineyard required to plant at least 60% Marsanne and Clairette; whites are prized as a pairing for bouillabaisse and seafood.
quote: one of the first AOCs in France, established in 1936, when the AOC system was first put in place... each vineyard must be planted with at least 60%... prized not only as a pairing for bouillabaisse but also as delightful aperitif wines and perfect accompaniments for many fish and seafood dishes.

claim: Cassis AOC covers just 215 hectares within the single commune of Cassis, producing roughly one million bottles annually split 67% white, 30% rose and 3% red, from Clairette, Marsanne and Ugni Blanc on limestone terraces beneath Cap Canaille.
quote: The appellation covers just 215 hectares within the single commune of Cassis, producing approximately one million bottles annually, with whites accounting for 67% of production, rosés 30%, and reds only 3%.

claim: The Cassis appellation comprises around 10-12 domaines on 215 hectares, 85% organic or in conversion, sheltered by Cap Canaille (Europe's highest sea cliff at ~400m); the tourism office lists estates including Domaine du Bagnol, Domaine du Paternel and Chateau de Fontcreuse plus tasting venues Divino and La Maison des Vins.
quote: Total Estates: 10 domaines... Vineyard Area: 215 hectares... Organic Status: 85% organic or in conversion... sheltered by Cap Canaille (Europe's highest sea cliff at ~400m)

claim: Clos Sainte Magdeleine farms 12 hectares of organic-certified terraced vineyards on the Cap Canaille cliffs beside the sea; guided tours followed by tasting run April-September Monday-Saturday at 11am and 4pm for groups of 20 at 10 euros per person, with the sales cellar open Tuesday-Saturday.
quote: Clos Sainte Magdeleine works 12 hectares of vineyards on exceptional terraced sites on the cliffs of Cap Canaille and beside the sea... Guided tours of the domain followed by a tasting are organized from April to September for groups of 20 people (from Monday to Saturday, at 11am and at 4pm, €10 per person).

claim: Domaine du Bagnol in Cassis is known for crisp white wines and has a charming wine room where a tasting of 5 different wines costs only 10 euros.
quote: Domaine du Bagnol (Cassis): Known for its crisp white wines. Domaine Du Barnol has a wonderfully charming wine room where the tasting of 5 different wines is only 10€.

claim: The Cassis vineyard is planted exclusively in the district of Cassis, sheltered by Cap Canaille, the tallest coastal cliff in France plunging 400 metres into the Mediterranean, and offers white, rose and red wines with tasting, tours and purchase opportunities.
quote: The Cassis vineyard is planted exclusively in the district of Cassis, sheltered by Cap Canaille, the tallest coastal cliff in France, plunging down from a height of 400 metres into the Mediterranean.

claim: Chateau de Fontcreuse, owned by the Brando family, has made famous Cassis whites since Colonel Teed bought it in 1922; its 38-hectare estate (26 ha in the Cassis AOC) produces a white blend of 60% Marsanne, 15% Clairette and 25% Ugni Blanc and has a tasting room in Cassis.
quote: In 1922, Colonel Teed... bought Chateau Fontcreuse... The Fontcreuse estate covers 38 hectares, 26 of which are in the Cassis appellation... The assemblage of Fontcreuse White Wine is composed of 60% Marsanne, 15% Clairette, 25% Ugni Blanc... the château has a tasting room in Cassis.

claim: Cassis tasting-room standouts include Clos Sainte Magdeleine for stunning sea views and excellent whites and Domaine du Bagnol for crisp whites, with the general advice that visitors should book tours and tastings in advance during peak season.
quote: Clos Sainte Magdeleine... stunning sea views and excellent whites... Domaine du Bagnol... Known for its crisp white wines... Many wineries offer tours and tastings, but it's best to book in advance, especially during peak season.
